manpage.title: ovn-ic
manpage.p: ovn-ic -- Open Virtual Network interconnection controller

ovn-ic, OVN interconnection controller, is a centralized daemon which communicates with global interconnection databases IC_NB/IC_SB to configure and exchange data with local NB/SB for interconnecting with other OVN deployments.

dl.dd: The OVSDB database containing the OVN Northbound Database. If the OVN_NB_DB environment variable is set, its value is used as the default. Otherwise, the default is unix:@RUNDIR@/ovnnb_db.sock.
The OVSDB database containing the OVN Southbound Database. If the OVN_SB_DB environment variable is set, its value is used as the default. Otherwise, the default is unix:@RUNDIR@/ovnsb_db.sock.

The OVSDB database containing the OVN Interconnection Northbound Database. If the OVN_IC_NB_DB environment variable is set, its value is used as the default. Otherwise, the default is unix:@RUNDIR@/ovn_ic_nb_db.sock.

The OVSDB database containing the OVN Interconnection Southbound Database. If the OVN_IC_SB_DB environment variable is set, its value is used as the default. Otherwise, the default is unix:@RUNDIR@/ovn_ic_sb_db.sock.

manpage.p: database in the above options must be an OVSDB active or passive connection method, as described in ovsdb(7).

Whoever can write to the interconnection databases can join any transit switch in them, advertise any route onto it and choose the tunnel key of its datapath. When the other availability zone is not trusted that far, give each one interconnection databases of its own and run one ovn-ic per pair against the same OVN Northbound and Southbound databases, each restricted with the options below. They come from the command line so that nothing in an interconnection database can change them.

dl.dd: Names this ovn-ic. It takes the Southbound lock ovn_ic_name instead of ovn_ic (characters a lock name cannot have are replaced by underscores), so several can be active at once. It records name as ic-instance in the other_config of the transit switches and remote chassis it creates and in the external_ids of the routes it learns, and it never modifies or deletes one that carries a different name, or none. Without this option ovn-ic owns exactly the ones that carry no name. When an instance is retired, what it created stays until it is removed by hand.
Serve only the transit switch name. Any other transit switch in the interconnection databases is ignored: no logical switch is created for it and its datapath is left alone.

The tunnel key of that transit switch's datapath, from the range reserved for transit switches. It replaces whatever another availability zone allocated or wrote. Give each instance a different key: the key is requested from the local ovn-northd, where two transit switches cannot share one. Requires --ic-transit-switch.

Accept gateways, transit switch ports and routes only from the availability zone name. Those of any other availability zone in the interconnection databases get no chassis and no port here, and their routes are not learned.

manpage.p: PKI configuration is required in order to use SSL/TLS for the connections to the Northbound and Southbound databases.

ovs-appctl can send commands to a running ovn-ic process. The currently supported commands are described below.
exit
Causes ovn-ic to gracefully terminate.
pause
Pauses the ovn-ic operation from processing any database changes. This will also instruct ovn-ic to drop any lock on SB DB.
resume
Resumes the ovn-ic operation to process database contents. This will also instruct ovn-northd to aspire for the lock on SB DB.
is-paused
Returns "true" if ovn-ic is currently paused, "false" otherwise.
status
Prints this server's status. Status will be "active" if ovn-ic has acquired OVSDB lock on SB DB, "standby" if it has not or "paused" if this instance is paused.

You may run ovn-ic more than once in an OVN deployment. When connected to a standalone or clustered DB setup, OVN will automatically ensure that only one of them is active at a time. If multiple instances of ovn-ic are running and the active ovn-ic fails, one of the hot standby instances of ovn-ic will automatically take over.
